title: Instruction List: the current result in a two-hand control
summary: Read an Instruction List program as one current result that each line combines with an operand, and use it to enable a press only when both hands are on the push buttons and the guard is closed.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show the response time, redundancy or fault behaviour a real two-hand safety device needs.
objectives: Read an Instruction List (IL) program as one current result that each instruction combines with an operand, from top to bottom.
Use LD, LDN, AND, XOR and ST to turn three inputs into three outputs.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/TwoHand.il each line is one instruction. LD loads an operand into the current result, LDN loads the opposite of an operand, AND combines the next operand with it, XOR is TRUE when exactly one of its two operands is TRUE, and ST stores the result in an output; the result stays in place after ST, so the next LD starts a new line of logic. PressEnable must be ON only with LeftHand, RightHand and GuardClosed all ON. GuardLamp must be ON when the guard is open. OneHandWarning must be ON when exactly one hand is on its button.
stages.checkpoint: You can say, for each output, the instructions that build its condition.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the three outputs at {{t:20}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:40}} ms. The inputs change every {{t:10}} ms, so work through one step at a time.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=true,TwoHand.GuardLamp=false,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=false@20|PressEnable ON only}} at {{t:20}} ms; {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=false,TwoHand.GuardLamp=true,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=false@30|GuardLamp ON only}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:TwoHand.PressEnable=false,TwoHand.GuardLamp=false,TwoHand.OneHandWarning=true@40|OneHandWarning ON only}} at {{t:40}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program turns PressEnable ON at {{t:10}} ms with only one hand on its button, and GuardLamp and OneHandWarning stay OFF whatever the inputs do. PressEnable must be ON only with both hands on their buttons and the guard closed, GuardLamp ON while the guard is open, and OneHandWarning ON while exactly one hand is on its button. Write the instructions yourself: the declarations are already there.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named TwoHand and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:20}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:40}} ms: the press is enabled once, at {{t:20}} ms, and switches off again at {{t:30}} ms when the guard opens.
stages.checkpoint: PressEnable rises at {{t:20}} ms and falls at {{t:30}} ms, and is never ON while GuardLamp is ON.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Once it passes, which input combinations does your PressEnable accept, and which one would a mistake that accepts a single hand let through?
stages.checkpoint: A two-hand control exists to keep both hands away from the press, so a condition that accepts one hand defeats it. Each line works on the result of the lines above it, which is why the order of the lines matters in IL.

hints.text: Look at the line that combines the second hand into PressEnable, and at what the two lamp outputs are given now. Each line works on the result of the lines above it.
LD LeftHand, AND RightHand, AND GuardClosed, ST PressEnable; LDN GuardClosed, ST GuardLamp; LD LeftHand, XOR RightHand, ST OneHandWarning.

faultCases: The starting program turns PressEnable ON at {{t:10}} ms with only one hand on its button, and GuardLamp and OneHandWarning stay OFF whatever the inputs do.
